oracle.note: Every case's oracle output below was produced by running the pinned released package on the documented graph and inputs. The recorded outputs were first produced in a temporary environment that was deleted after import and have since been reproduced by the retained locked generators named in generation. Disagreements and out-of-scope cases are recorded, never bent. The parity test parses each verbatim output: the verdict must equal oracle_result and the distributions the oracle's formula cites must equal the distributions our recorded proof cites; a named route is an agreement of a weaker class (agree_named_route).

generation.script_note: Each retained generator regenerates its cases through the packages' public API in an isolated locked environment (Ananke 0.5.0 on CPython 3.11; dosearch 1.0.12 on R 4.6.1) and compares verdict, formula and verbatim output with this file; it never rewrites the file. The Rust parity test still parses the recorded verbatim output rather than running an oracle.

reference_review.scope: Six cases of the Ananke OneLineGID/OneLineAID/OneLineID and dosearch 1.0.12 public APIs on one four-variable ADMG with two experiments, one ancestral-margin surrogate experiment and an observational-only specification, and four dosearch specifications (back-door, front-door, two-study mixed data, transportability with selection bias). The generators regenerate each verdict and printed formula; they do not check that a formula is numerically correct.
reference_review.independence_basis: The repository-authored Python and R harnesses pin the graphs, experiment sets and queries themselves, call only the public Ananke and dosearch entry points, and compare verdict, formula text and the recorded verbatim output with the fixture. They import no product code and read no product output or upstream source/test file. The Ananke experiment encoding (fix the treatments, restrict to the measured vertices) was established by exercising the public API until the recorded outputs were matched, so the encoding is the author's reading of the documented interface. The asserting Rust test additionally parses the recorded outputs and executes the product proofs against enumerated truth.
reference_review.historical_exposure: The original harnesses were deleted after the first import, so historical author exposure is unknown. The retained harnesses were written from the packages' public documentation and signatures; no upstream algorithm or test source was consulted or copied.
reference_review.redistribution: Ananke is Apache-2.0 and dosearch is GPL (>= 3); both, and their locked dependencies, remain isolated tooling outside the product runtime and ordinary CI. The repository retains its MIT OR Apache-2.0 harnesses, locks, scenario coordinates and the factual formula strings the packages printed, with no upstream source or tests.
reference_review.limitations: Six small fixed graphs. Agreement is on verdict and formula text; an alternative equivalent formula would be reported as a difference and not judged. The Ananke runtime is pinned older than current releases (scipy 1.11.4, numpy<2) for import compatibility. The product returns a named route or a weaker verdict on several cases (agreement classes are recorded per case) and the transportability and selection-bias case is out of scope for the product. This fixture establishes no estimation accuracy, uncertainty or calibration.

cases.note: The oracle (Ananke OneLineID.id()) returned False, i.e. proves non-identifiability from observational data; this search only reports that its frozen rule set found nothing (not_certified), which is compatible with but weaker than the oracle's verdict.

Data P(x,y,z): the theorem-scoped sID route identifies it before any generic search; dosearch returns the backdoor adjustment. agree (named route): the theorem-scoped sID route identifies it, so Antecedent returns the named route and no proof; nothing cites leaves to compare. Every term of the oracle's formula is a margin or conditional of the one input distribution.

agree (named route): the theorem-scoped sID route identifies it, so Antecedent returns the named route and no proof; nothing cites leaves to compare. Every term of the oracle's formula is a margin or conditional of the one input distribution.

Executed dosearch (data p(x,z) and p(z,y), graph x -> z -> y) identifies p(y|do(x)) = sum_z p(y|z) p(z|x). This search identifies the same query and cites both studies; its value is also checked against enumerated truth (crates/antecedent-estimate/tests/mixed_source_execution.rs).

Executed dosearch (transportability node t, selection node s) identifies the query. Needs selection-bias and transportability nodes as inputs: this route searches only the target population's whole-population studies (other populations and selected samples are excluded and listed), so it cannot express this case. Recorded, not shaped.
